diff.decisive: Every executable file, the install hook and the quoted jailbreak test document are byte-identical to 3.65.1. Both original suspicious rules also fired on 3.65.1 with the current rules.

behavior: Node ESM CLI loads local dist/main.js. Readable TypeScript output, local dashboard assets and bundled agent documents; no concealed executable delta.

postinstall reads local package/plugin versions, prints stale-plugin guidance and may detach the local board ensure command when a Claude plugin cache exists. CI/quiet/no-board/test controls suppress this startup. The board defaults to 127.0.0.1, has host/origin checks, and ensure probes health before starting a process.

Explicit install/upgrade commands clone the declared great_cto repository or run npm/pnpm/Volta for this package. Agent commands launch Claude/Codex for local development work. Optional board daemon registration uses user launchd/systemd/Task Scheduler state.

Telemetry is disabled by default. sendUsagePing checks environment/config opt-in before constructing the event and POSTing to telemetry.greatcto.systems. The stable identifier is SHA-256 of username/hostname, truncated to 8 hex characters. Files written by writeConfig contain telemetry settings, not raw host identity. The install-ping path is additionally filtered out by the command allowlist, which lacks install.

Codex auth.json reads inspect authentication mode/token presence for readiness reporting; prompts are sent on stdin to the Codex CLI. The LLM fallback sends an explicitly supplied API key to api.anthropic.com.

The suspicious override literals are a conditional refusal instruction and a categorized adversarial test seed. Each test case explicitly expects refusal or an error outcome. Markdown shell fences cause the document to be identified as shell.
Fetched GitHub page assets and Stryker originate from documentation links/command examples. They are not declared runtime dependencies of this dependency-free CLI package.

limits: Static review, not a deployment audit. No invocation-specific consent, operator configuration or runtime traffic was supplied. The verdict follows the actual implementation, documentary refusal context and release diff, not an absence of detections. The CLI has ordinary powerful developer-tool capabilities; no compromise was found.
